title: Acidification of the battlefield: how Pst manipulates apoplastic pH homeostasis to promote stripe rust disease in wheat
content: Plant–pathogen interactions have long been described as an evolutionary arms race, with both sides continuously developing new molecular strategies to gain the upper hand. If the plant is successful, it mounts effective defenses, and the interaction becomes “incompatible.” If the pathogen wins, it manipulates the plant to create a comfortable niche for itself, resulting in a “compatible” interaction and ultimately disease.
